tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). # Readings — datastack (DS-v1, non-normative; spec v0 §36, §38, §46, §47, §56, §58, Part XIV, §82)

Module: `formal/Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean` (namespace `Ern.Lib.DataStack`).
Machine-checked examples: section `Witness` of that module (`run_ok`, `reading_above`,
`reading_order`, `reading_mark`, `reading_grow_dst`, `reading_newStack`, `reading_rewind_right`,
all by `decide` on library-reachable states under `Access.Examples.K0`). Four scratch files outside
the repository, re-elaborated against `b4a5cd3`: `../final5/nostack.lean` (DS-R3),
`../final5/d17.lean` and `../../records-chk/q28split.lean` (DS-R13), `../../records-chk/okonly.lean`
(R3).

Source of the contract: the brief's obligation 6 (DS-v1). Spec v0 does not define it (Part XIV
preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and
are not defined here"). Every entry: clause, reading used, alternative, example whose verdict
changes. "[draft]" = the reading of the draft (`formal/derivability_0.1`, `Lib/DataStack.lean`),
used per policy ("use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings").

## Readings that change verdicts

**DS-R1 "a cell above m" [draft].** DS-v1: "rejects if an active authority derived from internal
covers a cell above m". Reading: the cells at positions `[m.top, top)` (`above`), those that
`rewind m` returns. Alternative A: any cell at position `≥ m.top`. Alternative B: the regions issued
after `m`. Example (`Witness.reading_above`, decided): after `rewind ⟨0,1,1⟩` (top 1) and the
program's `release(5)`, `derive(4, [3], Modify)` gives authority 8, active, derived from `internal`
4, on cell 3 (position 1 ≥ `m0.top` = 0, but ≥ current top). `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `ok` here; under
A it is rejected. Safety is unaffected: the next `push` over cell 3 is rejected by the effective
right (§43, §61.1). Under B, a block grown after `m` from a base below `m` blocks `rewind` on its
lower part too (draft `opsE4`; not re-run here).

**DS-R2 order of the dead/foreign-mark `fail` and of the right of §36 [draft].** §58: "static
preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract";
DS-v1 lists "fails on a dead or foreign mark" first and says nothing about §36. Reading: mark
liveness first (`fail`), then `AdminRight` (`reject`). Alternative: §36 first. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (1)): a callee frame with no right on the stack value rewinds to the
removed mark `⟨0,1,1⟩`: `fail` here, `reject` under the alternative. Consequence: `mark_no_aba`
gives `fail` unconditionally.

**DS-R3 "foreign" mark.** Reading: a mark is live for stack `j` iff `m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks`
(`LiveMark`); the stack identity is checked explicitly although, under `MarksWF` (proved on every
library-reachable state), membership alone implies it. The explicit identity check changes no verdict
on reachable states.
`rewind` on a stack index that does not exist is `reject` (no stack value) [draft]. This is a reason
to reject that DS-v1 does not list (narrow check ds4-2). Alternative: a mark of a stack that does not
exist is not live, so DS-v1's "fails on a dead or foreign mark" gives `fail`; or DS-v1 is silent.
Example (`../final5/nostack.lean`): on the initial state `d0` (`DReach.init`, no stack),
`rewind(0, ⟨0,0,0⟩)` is `reject` through `RewindStep.noStack` and neither `ok` nor `fail`; `fail` under
the alternative.

**DS-R4 `grow` with `extra = 0` [draft].** DS-v1 says nothing. Reading: `reject` ("grow" means a
larger size). Alternative: an in-place re-issue of the same region. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (2)): `grow(0, 5, 0)` in `d9` is `reject`, while release, static checks,
in-place check, `split` and `store` of the same region are all `ok` (alternative: `ok`).

**DS-R5 `grow` of a live block that cannot extend in place: `fail`** (libs.md C10; DS-v1 "fail
otherwise"). The draft rejected it. Reading: the in-place check (`InPlace`: the block ends at the top
and `extra` cells follow) is the availability check of the derived issue (§77.4) and gives `fail`.
Example (`Witness.run_ok`): `grow(0, 5, 1)` in `d7`, where block 6 lies above block 5, is `fail`.
A `b` that is no block of the stack (`Stack.block` gives none): DS-v1 says nothing. Reading [draft
`case_grow`]: `reject` (`GrowStep.noBlock`). Alternative: `fail`, by analogy with DS-v1 "rewind m
fails on a dead or foreign mark" (an identifier the stack does not record). Example
(`Ern.Corpus.DataStack.DS03`, conjunct `GrowStep K0 0 6 1 ds03 .reject`, decided): after
`grow(0, 6, 1)` replaced block 6 by block 9 (`ds03.stacks` records the blocks `[⟨0, 3, 9, 5⟩]`
only), `grow(0, 6, 1)` is `reject` here and `fail` under the alternative (the step reaches
`noBlock` and no other rule).

**DS-R6 order inside `grow`.** The derived issue's static checks (`IssueStatic`) cannot be read on
the state before the release of `b` (the destination still holds `b`, §77.2 "holding no active
authority"). Reading: block lookup and `0 < extra` (`reject`); `release(b)` (`reject` if refused);
`IssueStatic` on the released state (`reject`); `InPlace` (`fail`, the state unchanged); `split`;
`store`. Alternative: in-place `fail` before the release. Changes the verdict when `b` cannot be
released and the block is not in place (`reject` here, `fail` under the alternative).

**DS-R7 `push` without room: `fail` [draft].** DS-v1 says only that `push` uses the derived issue.
Reading: the `size` cells at the top must exist (`top + size ≤ |cells|`); otherwise `fail`
(availability, §77.4), checked after `IssueStatic` on the requested cells that exist. Alternative:
"region belongs to the administered storage" (§77.2, static) gives `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (3)): `push(0, 3, 4)` on a stack of 2 cells is `fail`.

**DS-R8 `push` static checks are those of the derived issue (`Arena.IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2).**
Not the draft's restricted ones: an `Init` destination is not rejected (spec v0 §77.2, O8.2).
`push` of size 0 is accepted (issue of the empty region): the empty block blocks no `rewind`, and
`rewind` forgets it in the metadata while its authority stays active [draft DS-3].

**DS-R9 `newStack` preconditions: §76.5 applies [draft]** (was R5; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says nothing about creation. Reading: those of `newArena` other than its guard
(`Arena.NewArenaBase`: §76.1–§76.3 and §76.5 "All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are
already `Init`", read for a stack) and `Guard56 (stackInternals :: others)` (§56). Alternative: drop
§76.5 for a stack (DS-v1 does not take over `newArena`). Same choice as H-R8 for pools. Example
(`Witness.reading_newStack`, decided on the initial state of statics `wsu`): leaf 0, `Uninit`, owns
the storage leaf 1 and so holds its root authority 1 (§47); `newStack(1, 1)` is `reject` (only
§76.5 fails: every other field of `NewArenaBase` and the guard hold), `ok` under the alternative.

**DS-R10 `mark` requires no right [draft]** (was R6; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1 says nothing about
a right for `mark`. Reading: `ok` on an existing stack, `reject` on a missing one; `mark` changes
library metadata only and creates no right (§36 ¶2, §38). Alternative: §36 ¶1, metadata is modified
"to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts", so `mark` needs a right on the
stack value (`AdminRight`, or a valid `writeShared` over it, §68), else `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_mark`): in `d13` (a callee frame entered after the rewind), the callee has no
`AdminRight`, no `Observe` right on the stack value 0 and no valid `writeShared` over it through any
authority; `mark(0)` is `ok` (a mark appended), `reject` under the alternative.

**DS-R11 `grow` destination: the recorded `Blk.dst` [draft]** (was R7; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says only "grow is in place only" and "uses the derived issue"; it does not name the destination.
Reading: the destination recorded for the block at `push` (`Blk.dst`), even when the block value has
been transferred since and that place is `Moved`. Alternative: the place that currently holds `b`.
Changes the arrival state. Example (`Witness.reading_grow_dst`): after the first push (block 5
stored at place 4), the program's `transfer(4, 5)` (§63) moves authority 5 to place 5 and makes
place 4 `Moved` (`d14`). `grow(0, 5, 1)` is `ok` and stores the new block authority 6 into place 4,
which becomes `Init` (§65), while place 5 keeps the released authority 5 (`d15`). Under the
alternative, the static checks of the derived issue (`IssueStatic`) and `store(6, 5)` are `ok` on
the same released and split state, and authority 6 is held by place 5.

**DS-R12 reasons for which `rewind` rejects: §36 applies** (B47). DS-v1: "rewind m fails on a
dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m,
otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it". It names one
reason to reject. Reading: §36 applies too (normative: `MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on
the stack value; the abstraction adds no rights to the kernel), so `rewind` rejects without
`AdminRight`. On library-reachable states and for an existing stack, this is the only reason outside
DS-v1's list (`rewind_ok_iff`, R3; that `ok` is then the only outcome is stated by `RewindStep.det` since `b2dcaa9`; before, it
follows from `Guarded.det`, R3). A stack index with no stack gives `reject` for another reason
outside the list, `RewindStep.noStack` (DS-R3). Alternative: DS-v1's list is exhaustive, so
`rewind` is `ok` whenever the mark is live and no such authority covers a cell above it. Example (`Witness.reading_rewind_right`,
decided): `d16` is reached by the rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩`, the program's `release(5)` and a callee frame
with no parameter or local. There, mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0 and no active authority
derived from `internal` 4 covers cell 2, the cell above it. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` here and
`ok` under the alternative. The kernel sequence cannot realize the alternative: `split` of
`internal` also rejects in `d16`, because `internal` is not exercisable at `Modify` (§61.1).
`AdminRight` has two conjuncts. `d16` tests only `MetaRight` (`internal` is active there); the other
conjunct, `internal` active, is DS-R13.

**DS-R13 a live mark of a dead stack** (narrow check ds4-3). DS-v1: "the stack keeps the ordered list
of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark". It does not speak of a dead stack. §46:
"The arena is **live** if `internal` is active", read for a stack by `AdminRight`. Reading:
`reject` (`RewindStep.static`), forced by the §61.1 check of the derived reset; also by the
`Active internal` conjunct of `AdminRight`. Alternative 1: DS-v1's list is exhaustive (the DS-R12
alternative): `ok`. Alternative 2: a mark of a dead stack is a dead mark: `fail` (under the DS-R2 order the mark is
checked first). Example (`../final5/d17.lean`: `d17_facts`, `d17_only_reject`): `d17` is `d11` (the
rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩` and the program's `release(5)`) followed by the program's `release(4)` of
`internal` 4. Mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0, no active authority derived from `internal` covers
cell 2, `MetaRight` still holds and `internal` is inactive. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` and nothing
else here, `ok` under alternative 1 and `fail` under alternative 2. The kernel sequence cannot
realize alternative 1: in `d17`, `split` of `internal` rejects because `internal` is inactive (§61.1;
`SplitPre.active`, the same test as the first conjunct of `AdminRight`). Without that conjunct the
outcome stays `reject` through `RewindStep.split` (`../../records-chk/q28split.lean`,
`d17_split_rejects`). So whether the liveness of the stack is part of the §36 check does not change
the verdict. The only alternatives that change it are alternative 2 (`fail`) and alternative 1
(`ok`), and alternative 1 is possible only if `rewind` skips the derived reset.

## Readings that change no accepted program (representation)

- **R1 State.** `DState = ⟨kern, stacks, fresh⟩`, separate from `S3` (§38, §46); a stack is its
  registry index, stacks are never removed; `fresh` is a global counter (§9 "a monotonically
  increasing counter is one possible representation"). The arena registry is not in `DState`: the
  guard reads it through the parameter `others` (§56), as `Arena.NewArenaPre` reads stacks through
  its `others`.
- **R2 Available cells** = positions `≥ top` of the ordered cells (`Stack.entry.available =
  cells.drop top`); `push` and `grow` take cells at the top only and `rewind` returns exactly
  `above`, so this is a set of leaves as in §46.
- **R3 `rewind` kernel part [draft]:** the derived reset of Part XIV restricted to `above st m`:
  `split(internal, [above])` then `release` of the new authority. Plus an explicit §36 check
  (`AdminRight`: `internal` active and `MetaRight` on the stack value) before the split, like
  `IssueStatic.live/metaRight`. **Exact outcome** (`rewind_ok_iff`, hypothesis: the state
  invariant `DReach` only, no `KInv`, no I3): for an existing stack, `rewind m` has an `ok` outcome iff `m` is
  live for the stack (DS-v1), `AdminRight` holds (§36), and no active authority derived from
  `internal` covers a cell of `above st m` (DS-v1). The model does not check the DS-v1 condition
  explicitly. It is the effective `Modify` of `internal` that `split` requires (§61.1, effective
  mode of §43; §61.3 follows). No other check of `split` or `release` rejects on such a state:
  - `internal` has own mode `Modify` and covers the cells (`DReach.stackShape`: §76.2 and §76.3 at
    `newStack`, kept by every step since modes and footprints never change, §42);
  - every anchor names an existing authority (`dBound_of_reachable`), so the fresh authority
    anchors no place (§62.3, §62.4).

  That `ok` is then the only outcome is stated by `RewindStep.det` (`b2dcaa9`); it follows from `Guarded.det`
  (scratch proof `../../records-chk/okonly.lean`, `rewind_only_ok`). With that exclusivity, for an
  existing stack, the only rejection outside DS-v1's list is §36 (DS-R12, DS-R13); a missing
  stack gives `reject` through `noStack` (DS-R3). Not proved here: whether the explicit
  §36 check ever rejects when the `split` check of §61.1 (`internal` active and exercisable at
  `Modify`) would accept.
- **R4 "removes m and every mark above it":** "above" = later in the ordered list;
  `marks := takeWhile (· ≠ m)`. Blocks with base `≥ m.top` are forgotten [draft].
- **R5, R6, R7:** moved to DS-R9, DS-R10, DS-R11 above (they change verdicts or arrival states;
  review round 2, DS-1).
- **R8 Library runs:** `DStep.kernel` admits any kernel step of non-administrative code.

4	/-!
5	# DataStack: a library administrative abstraction (contract DS-v1, non-normative)
6	
7	A `DataStack` instance of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`. The spec does not define
8	its contract (Part XIV preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their
9	library abstractions and are not defined here"). The contract formalized here is the library
10	contract **DS-v1**, which is **not normative**: every definition below that encodes a DS-v1 item
11	says so. The normative clauses that constrain it are §36 (`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable
12	on the stack value; the abstraction adds no rights to the kernel), §38 and §46 (library state
13	separate from `S₃`), §47 (empty initial registry), §56 (guard over all registries of live
14	administrations) and §58 (outcomes).
15	
16	DS-v1: marks carry the stack identity and a fresh mark identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list
17	of live marks; `rewind m` fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived
18	from `internal` covers a cell above `m`, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes `m`
19	and every mark above it; `push` and `grow` use the derived `issue` of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`: its
20	static checks, the availability `fail`, then `split` of `internal` and `store` of the block); `grow`
21	is in place only (same base, extension into the space directly after the block, `fail` otherwise).
22	
23	Every `ok` step of the library is a sequence of kernel steps O1–O16 (`DReach.reachable`), so the
24	abstraction adds no rights to the kernel (§36).
25	-/
26	
27	namespace Ern.Lib.DataStack
28	
29	open Ern.MemoryModel Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena
30	
31	/-! ## Library state (DS-v1; §38, §46, §47) -/
32	
33	/-- A block issued by a stack (DS-v1, non-normative; recorded like the issuances of §46): position
34	`base` of its first cell and number `size` of cells among the ordered cells of the stack, block
35	authority `auth`, destination `dst` that received it. -/
36	structure Blk where
37	  base : Nat
38	  size : Nat
39	  auth : Nat
40	  dst : Nat
41	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
42	
43	/-- A mark (DS-v1, non-normative: "marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier";
44	library metadata of an administrative abstraction, §36, §38): the identity of its stack, its fresh
45	identifier, the top of the stack when it was taken. -/
46	structure Mark where
47	  stack : Nat
48	  id : Nat
49	  top : Nat
50	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
51	
52	/-- A stack (DS-v1, non-normative; library state, §38, §46): administered storage, `internal`
53	authority held by the stack value (§36), ordered cells (the leaves of the storage at creation),
54	top (the cells at positions `≥ top` are available), issued blocks (oldest first), and the ordered
55	list of live marks (DS-v1: "the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks"). -/
56	structure Stack where
57	  storage : Nat
58	  internal : Nat
59	  cells : List Nat
60	  top : Nat
61	  blocks : List Blk
62	  marks : List Mark
63	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
64	
65	/-- State of the stack library (DS-v1, non-normative; §38: administrative states of library
66	abstractions are separate from `S₃`): the kernel state, the stack registry (a stack is identified
67	by its index; stacks are never removed) and the next fresh mark identifier. -/
68	structure DState where
69	  kern : S3
70	  stacks : List Stack
71	  fresh : Nat
72	
73	/-- Initial state (§47: the kernel's initial state; the library registry starts empty; DS-v1,
74	non-normative: no mark identifier given out). -/
75	def DState.init (statics : Statics) : DState := ⟨S3.init statics, [], 0⟩
76	
77	/-- The `n` cells from position `b` of the stack, leaves of the administered storage (§46; DS-v1,
78	non-normative). -/
79	def cellsOf (st : Stack) (b n : Nat) : List Nat := (st.cells.drop b).take n
80	
81	/-- The cells above mark `m` (DS-v1, non-normative, "a cell above m"; reading recorded; §46
82	available leaves): the positions from the top of `m` to the current top, those that `rewind m`
83	returns to available. -/
84	def above (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : List Nat := cellsOf st m.top (st.top - m.top)
85	
86	/-- The stack seen as an administration entry (§46, §36; DS-v1, non-normative): storage,
87	`internal`, available cells (positions `≥ top`) and issued blocks. Used for `MetaRight` and the
88	static checks of the derived `issue`, which read only the storage and `internal`. -/
89	def Stack.entry (st : Stack) : ArenaEntry :=
90	  ⟨st.storage, st.internal, st.cells.drop st.top,
91	    st.blocks.map fun x => (cellsOf st x.base x.size, x.auth)⟩
92	
93	/-- The block of the stack whose authority is `b` (§46 issuances; DS-v1, non-normative). -/
94	def Stack.block (st : Stack) (b : Nat) : Option Blk := st.blocks.find? fun y => decide (y.auth = b)
95	
96	/-- A live mark of stack `j` (DS-v1, non-normative: a mark that is neither dead nor foreign; it
97	decides the `fail` case of `rewind`, §58): it names stack `j` and belongs to its list of live
98	marks. -/
99	def LiveMark (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Prop := m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks
100	
101	/-- Decidability of `LiveMark` (§58; DS-v1). -/
102	instance (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Decidable (LiveMark j st m) := by
103	  unfold LiveMark; infer_instance
104	
105	/-- The administrative right of §36 for a stack (DS-v1, non-normative, with §36 and §46 read for a
106	stack): the stack is live (`internal` is active) and `MetaRight`, `Modify` exercisable on the stack
107	value, the place holding `internal`. -/
108	def AdminRight (s : S3) (st : Stack) : Prop := s.Active st.internal ∧ MetaRight s st.entry
109	
110	/-- Decidability of `AdminRight` (§36; DS-v1). -/
111	instance (s : S3) (st : Stack) : Decidable (AdminRight s st) := by
112	  unfold AdminRight; infer_instance
113	
114	/-! ## `newStack` and the guard of §56 -/
115	
116	/-- The stack registry as a registry of live administrations (§56; DS-v1, non-normative): the
117	`internal` identities of its live stacks. -/
118	def stackInternals (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) : List Nat :=
119	  (stacks.filter fun st => decide (s.Active st.internal)).map (·.internal)
120	
121	/-- Preconditions of `newStack(storage, internal)` (DS-v1, non-normative; §56): those of `newArena`
122	other than its guard (`NewArenaBase`, §76.1–§76.3 and §76.5 read for a stack), and the guard of §56
123	over the stack registry and every other registry of live administrations `others`. -/
124	structure NewStackPre (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) (others : List (List Nat))
125	    (storage internal : Nat) : Prop where
126	  /-- §76.1–§76.3, §76.5, read for a stack (DS-v1). -/
127	  base : NewArenaBase s storage internal
128	  /-- §56: no live administration of any registry uses `internal`. -/
129	  guard : Guard56 (stackInternals s stacks :: others) internal
130	
131	/-- Decidability of `NewStackPre` (§56; DS-v1). -/
132	instance (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) :
133	    Decidable (NewStackPre s stacks others storage internal) :=
134	  decidable_of_iff (NewArenaBase s storage internal ∧
135	    Guard56 (stackInternals s stacks :: others) internal)
136	    ⟨fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩, fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩⟩
137	
138	/-- Effect of `newStack` (DS-v1, non-normative; §36: registration adds no rights): a stack whose
139	cells are the leaves of the storage, top 0, no block, no mark; the kernel state is unchanged. -/
140	def newStackEff (D : DState) (storage internal : Nat) : DState :=
141	  { D with stacks := D.stacks ++ [⟨storage, internal, footprint D.kern.P storage, 0, [], []⟩] }
142	
143	/-- `newStack` as a relation (DS-v1, non-normative; §56, §58): `ok` or `reject`. -/
144	def NewStackStep (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) (D : DState) :
145	    Outcome3 DState → Prop :=
146	  Guarded (NewStackPre D.kern D.stacks others storage internal) (newStackEff D storage internal)
147	
148	/-! ## `push` (DS-v1: the derived `issue`, Part XIV, §77) -/
149	
150	/-- Metadata after `push` (DS-v1, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §77 on §46 metadata): the
151	cells leave the available part (the top rises by `size`), the block is recorded. -/
152	def pushMeta (st : Stack) (size a dst : Nat) : Stack :=
153	  { st with top := st.top + size, blocks := st.blocks ++ [⟨st.top, size, a, dst⟩] }
154	
155	/-- `push(j, size, dst)` (DS-v1, non-normative: "push uses the derived issue"): the derived `issue`
156	of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`) of the `size` cells at the top into `dst`, on the stack seen as an
157	entry: its static checks (`IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2, with `MetaRight` of §36), then `fail`, the
158	state unchanged, when fewer than `size` cells are left (availability, §77.4; reading recorded),
159	then `split` of `internal` on the cells (O2) and `store` of the block, of fresh identity `|A|`, into
160	`dst` (O8). -/
161	inductive PushStep (k : K) (j size dst : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
162	  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
163	  | static {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
164	      ¬ IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
165	  | fail {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
166	      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
167	      ¬ st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length → PushStep k j size dst D .fail
168	  | split {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
169	      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
170	      st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length →
171	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size] D.kern .reject →
172	      PushStep k j size dst D .reject
173	  | store {st : Stack} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
174	      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
175	      st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length →
176	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
177	      StoreStep D.kern.A.length dst s₁ .reject → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
178	  | ok {st : Stack} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
179	      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
180	      st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length →
181	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
182	      StoreStep D.kern.A.length dst s₁ (.ok s₂) →
183	      PushStep k j size dst D
184	        (.ok ⟨s₂, D.stacks.set j (pushMeta st size D.kern.A.length dst), D.fresh⟩)
185	
186	/-! ## `mark` (DS-v1) -/
187	
188	/-- Metadata after `mark` (DS-v1, non-normative; library metadata, §36, §38): a mark naming stack
189	`j`, with the fresh identifier `fresh` and the current top, is appended to the live marks. -/
190	def markMeta (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (fresh : Nat) : Stack :=
191	  { st with marks := st.marks ++ [⟨j, fresh, st.top⟩] }
192	
193	/-- `mark(j)` (DS-v1, non-normative; §58 outcomes; §36: metadata only, no right created): `ok`
194	on an existing stack; the identifier is fresh. -/
195	inductive MarkStep (j : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
196	  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → MarkStep j D .reject
197	  | ok {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
198	      MarkStep j D (.ok ⟨D.kern, D.stacks.set j (markMeta j st D.fresh), D.fresh + 1⟩)
199	
200	/-! ## `rewind` (DS-v1) -/
201	
202	/-- Metadata after `rewind m` (DS-v1, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §78 on §46 metadata):
203	the cells above `m` return to available (the top returns to the top of `m`), the blocks from that
204	top are forgotten, `m` and every later mark are removed. -/
205	def rewindMeta (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Stack :=
206	  { st with
207	    top := m.top
208	    blocks := st.blocks.filter fun x => decide (x.base < m.top)
209	    marks := st.marks.takeWhile fun x => decide (x ≠ m) }
210	
211	/-- `rewind(j, m)` (DS-v1, non-normative): `fail`, the state unchanged, on a dead or foreign mark;
212	`reject` without the administrative right of §36; then the derived `reset` of Part XIV on the cells
213	above `m` (reading recorded): `split` of `internal` on them (O2), which rejects when an active
214	authority derived from `internal` covers one of them (`rewind_rejects_live_above`), and `release`
215	of the derived authority (O3); `ok`: the cells return to available, `m` and the later marks are
216	removed. -/
217	inductive RewindStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (m : Mark) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
218	  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → RewindStep k j m D .reject
219	  | dead {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → ¬ LiveMark j st m → RewindStep k j m D .fail
220	  | static {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark j st m → ¬ AdminRight D.kern st →
221	      RewindStep k j m D .reject
222	  | split {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark j st m → AdminRight D.kern st →
223	      SplitStep k st.internal [above st m] D.kern .reject → RewindStep k j m D .reject
224	  | release {st : Stack} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark j st m →
225	      AdminRight D.kern st → SplitStep k st.internal [above st m] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
226	      ReleaseStep D.kern.A.length s₁ .reject → RewindStep k j m D .reject
227	  | ok {st : Stack} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark j st m →
228	      AdminRight D.kern st → SplitStep k st.internal [above st m] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
229	      ReleaseStep D.kern.A.length s₁ (.ok s₂) →
230	      RewindStep k j m D (.ok ⟨s₂, D.stacks.set j (rewindMeta st m), D.fresh⟩)
231	
232	/-- `rewind` has one outcome (§58: a guarded transition has one outcome; DS-v1, non-normative):
233	the cases of `RewindStep` exclude each other, and `split` and `release` are deterministic
234	(`Guarded.det`). With `rewind_ok_iff`, an `ok` rewind is never also `reject` or `fail`. -/
235	theorem RewindStep.det {k : K} {j : Nat} {m : Mark} {D : DState} {o₁ o₂ : Outcome3 DState}
236	    (h₁ : RewindStep k j m D o₁) (h₂ : RewindStep k j m D o₂) : o₁ = o₂ := by
237	  cases h₁ with
238	  | noStack h =>
239	    cases h₂ with
240	    | noStack _ => rfl
241	    | dead h' _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'
242	    | static _ _ _ => rfl
243	    | split _ _ _ _ => rfl
244	    | release _ _ _ _ _ => rfl
245	    | ok h' _ _ _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'
246	  | dead h hl =>
247	    cases h₂ with
248	    | noStack h' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'
249	    | dead _ _ => rfl
250	    | static h' hl' _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl' hl
251	    | split h' hl' _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl' hl
252	    | release h' hl' _ _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl' hl
253	    | ok h' hl' _ _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl' hl
254	  | static h hl ha =>
255	    cases h₂ with
256	    | noStack _ => rfl
257	    | dead h' hl' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl hl'
258	    | static _ _ _ => rfl
259	    | split _ _ _ _ => rfl
260	    | release _ _ _ _ _ => rfl
261	    | ok h' _ ha' _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd ha' ha
262	  | split h hl _ hs =>
263	    cases h₂ with
264	    | noStack _ => rfl
265	    | dead h' hl' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl hl'
266	    | static _ _ _ => rfl
267	    | split _ _ _ _ => rfl
268	    | release _ _ _ _ _ => rfl
269	    | ok h' _ _ hs' _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; cases Guarded.det hs hs'
270	  | release h hl _ hs hr =>
271	    cases h₂ with
272	    | noStack _ => rfl
273	    | dead h' hl' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl hl'
274	    | static _ _ _ => rfl
275	    | split _ _ _ _ => rfl
276	    | release _ _ _ _ _ => rfl
277	    | ok h' _ _ hs' hr' =>
278	      rw [h] at h'; cases h'; cases Guarded.det hs hs'; cases Guarded.det hr hr'
279	  | ok h hl ha hs hr =>
280	    cases h₂ with
281	    | noStack h' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'
282	    | dead h' hl' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl hl'
283	    | static h' _ ha' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd ha ha'
284	    | split h' _ _ hs' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; cases Guarded.det hs hs'
285	    | release h' _ _ hs' hr' =>
286	      rw [h] at h'; cases h'; cases Guarded.det hs hs'; cases Guarded.det hr hr'
287	    | ok h' _ _ hs' hr' =>
288	      rw [h] at h'; cases h'; cases Guarded.det hs hs'; cases Guarded.det hr hr'; rfl
289	
290	/-! ## `grow` (DS-v1: in place, the derived `issue`) -/
291	
292	/-- In-place extension (DS-v1, non-normative: "extension into the space directly after the
293	block"; the availability check of the derived `issue`, §77.4): the block ends at the top, and
294	`extra` available cells follow it. -/
295	def InPlace (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra : Nat) : Prop :=
296	  x.base + x.size = st.top ∧ st.top + extra ≤ st.cells.length
297	
298	/-- Decidability of `InPlace` (§77.4; DS-v1). -/
299	instance (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra : Nat) : Decidable (InPlace st x extra) := by
300	  unfold InPlace; infer_instance
301	
302	/-- The grown block (DS-v1, non-normative: same base, `extra` more cells, new authority `a`, same
303	destination; an issuance of §46). -/
304	def growBlk (x : Blk) (extra a : Nat) : Blk := ⟨x.base, x.size + extra, a, x.dst⟩
305	
306	/-- Metadata after `grow` (DS-v1, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §77 on §46 metadata): the
307	top rises by `extra`; the block is replaced by the grown block. -/
308	def growMeta (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra a : Nat) : Stack :=
309	  { st with
310	    top := st.top + extra
311	    blocks := st.blocks.map fun y => if y.auth = x.auth then growBlk x extra a else y }
312	
313	/-- `grow(j, b, extra)` (DS-v1, non-normative: in place only, using the derived `issue`): `reject`
314	when `b` is not a block of the stack or `extra` is zero (reading recorded); `release` of `b` (O3);
315	then the derived `issue` of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`) of the region of the same base and of size
316	`size + extra` into the recorded destination, on the released state: its static checks
317	(`IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2), `fail`, the state unchanged, unless the extension is in place
318	(DS-v1 "fail otherwise", availability §77.4), `split` of `internal` (O2) and `store` of the new
319	block (O8). -/
320	inductive GrowStep (k : K) (j b extra : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
321	  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
322	  | noBlock {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = none →
323	      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
324	  | noExtra {st : Stack} {x : Blk} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x → extra = 0 →
325	      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
326	  | release {st : Stack} {x : Blk} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x → 0 < extra →
327	      ReleaseStep b D.kern .reject → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
328	  | static {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
329	      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
330	      ¬ IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst →
331	      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
332	  | fail {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
333	      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
334	      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst →
335	      ¬ InPlace st x extra → GrowStep k j b extra D .fail
336	  | split {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
337	      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
338	      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst → InPlace st x extra →
339	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ .reject →
340	      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
341	  | store {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
342	      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
343	      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst → InPlace st x extra →
344	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ (.ok s₂) →
345	      StoreStep s₁.A.length x.dst s₂ .reject → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
346	  | ok {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ s₂ s₃ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
347	      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
348	      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst → InPlace st x extra →
349	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ (.ok s₂) →
350	      StoreStep s₁.A.length x.dst s₂ (.ok s₃) →
351	      GrowStep k j b extra D (.ok ⟨s₃, D.stacks.set j (growMeta st x extra s₁.A.length), D.fresh⟩)
352	
353	/-! ## Library runs (DS-v1; §36, §56, §57) -/
354	
355	/-- One `ok` step of the stack library (DS-v1, non-normative): a kernel step O1–O16 of
356	non-administrative code, the registry unchanged; `newStack` with the guard of §56 against the other
357	registries `others`; `push`, `mark`, `rewind`, `grow`. -/
358	inductive DStep (k : K) : DState → DState → Prop where
359	  | kernel {D : DState} {s' : S3} : KStep k D.kern s' → DStep k D ⟨s', D.stacks, D.fresh⟩
360	  | newStack {D D' : DState} {others : List (List Nat)} {storage i : Nat} :
361	      NewStackStep others storage i D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
362	  | push {D D' : DState} {j size dst : Nat} : PushStep k j size dst D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
363	  | mark {D D' : DState} {j : Nat} : MarkStep j D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
364	  | rewind {D D' : DState} {j : Nat} {m : Mark} : RewindStep k j m D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
365	  | grow {D D' : DState} {j b extra : Nat} : GrowStep k j b extra D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
366	
367	/-- States reachable from the initial state by library steps (DS-v1, non-normative; §47). -/
368	inductive DReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : DState → Prop where
369	  | init : DReach k statics (DState.init statics)
370	  | step {D D' : DState} : DReach k statics D → DStep k D D' → DReach k statics D'
371	
372	/-- Finite sequences of library steps (DS-v1, non-normative; §58 `ok` transitions). -/
373	inductive DRun (k : K) : DState → DState → Prop where
374	  | refl (D : DState) : DRun k D D
375	  | tail {D D' D'' : DState} : DRun k D D' → DStep k D' D'' → DRun k D D''
376	
377	/-- The kernel part of a library step is reached by kernel steps (§36: the abstraction adds no
378	rights to the kernel; Part XIV: `issue` is `split` then `store`, the reset part of `rewind` is
379	`split` then `release`; DS-v1). -/
380	theorem DStep.reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D D' : DState}
381	    (hr : Reachable k statics D.kern) (h : DStep k D D') : Reachable k statics D'.kern := by
382	  cases h with
383	  | kernel hk => exact .step hr hk
384	  | newStack hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact hr
385	  | push hs =>
386	    cases hs with
387	    | ok _ _ _ hsp hst => exact .step (.step hr (.split hsp)) (.store hst)
388	  | mark hs => cases hs with | ok _ => exact hr
389	  | rewind hs =>
390	    cases hs with
391	    | ok _ _ _ hsp hrl => exact .step (.step hr (.split hsp)) (.release hrl)
392	  | grow hs =>
393	    cases hs with
394	    | ok _ _ _ hrl _ _ hsp hst =>
395	      exact .step (.step (.step hr (.release hrl)) (.split hsp)) (.store hst)
396	
397	/-- The kernel state of every library-reachable state is kernel-reachable (§36, §57; DS-v1). -/
398	theorem DReach.reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (h : DReach k statics D) :
399	    Reachable k statics D.kern := by
400	  induction h with
401	  | init => exact .init
402	  | step _ hs ih => exact hs.reachable ih
403	
404	/-! ## Helper lemmas (lists, kernel effects) -/
405	
406	/-- Reading a list after `set` (support for the §46 metadata updates of DS-v1). -/
407	theorem getElem?_set_cases {α : Type} {l : List α} {j i : Nat} {v x : α}
408	    (h : (l.set j v)[i]? = some x) : (i = j ∧ x = v) ∨ (i ≠ j ∧ l[i]? = some x) := by
409	  rw [List.getElem?_set] at h
410	  by_cases hij : j = i
411	  · subst hij; simp only [↓reduceIte] at h; split at h
412	    · cases h; exact .inl ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
413	    · cases h
414	  · simp only [hij, ↓reduceIte] at h; exact .inr ⟨Ne.symm hij, h⟩
415	
416	/-- Reading a list after appending one element (support for the §46 metadata updates of
417	DS-v1). -/
418	theorem getElem?_append_single {α : Type} {l : List α} {x y : α} {i : Nat}
419	    (h : (l ++ [x])[i]? = some y) : l[i]? = some y ∨ y = x := by

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

----
## 36. Shared Mutation and Internal Administration

An abstraction may keep its metadata in `SharedMutable` storage and modify it through `writeShared` to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts. **Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant the right to create, recycle, or terminate exclusive authority over the administered storage.** Such operations require `internal` to be exercisable in `Modify` mode from the value administering the storage.

For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**. The `writeShared` branch alone is insufficient. `MetaRight` governs the creation or recycling of authorities over existing storage; it does not govern the creation of a fresh allocation by `alloc` (Section 71). Concurrency between calls belongs to Spec 2. Operations issuing, recycling, ending, or invalidating regions must preserve active authorities and dependencies. Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations: any synchronized implementation of it belongs to Spec 2. These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel.

----
## 38. Machine State

The access discipline is based on the finite state

\[ S_3=(F,P,I,A,D) \]

where `F` represents the frame stack, `P` the places, `I` their initialization, `A` the authorities, and `D` the validity anchors. Administrative states of arenas and other library abstractions are separate from `S₃`. The external contract `K` is a separate parameter. The internal representation may carry auxiliary information that creates no new rights.

## 39. Execution Frames

## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The ownership graph of statics is acyclic: no static is owned, directly or transitively, by itself. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract

`K` contains the predicates `DeclaredDisjoint`, `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone`, `Deallocable`, `FreeCompat`, and `Satisfiable`. Their obligations are specified in Section 80. `K` can neither fabricate access rights nor remove an obligation of the Charter. The predicate `Invalidates` is not part of this contract.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 58. Transition Outcomes

Every operation has a conceptual outcome among:

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.

An `ok` transition must satisfy its preconditions, apply exactly its prescribed effects, and preserve the relevant invariants. No transition fabricates a permission to make its conclusion true. Holder and anchor changes are evaluated in the **resulting state** when a rule explicitly so provides.

# XIV. Arenas and Collective Invalidation — Reference Abstraction

An arena is a **library abstraction**, not a memory-kernel primitive. Operations O17 through O19 are **derived** from operations O1 through O16 and abstraction-specific metadata: `newArena` registers an administration without modifying the kernel; `issue` performs `split` followed by `store` (after checking availability); `reset` performs a `Modify` derivation over all storage—through `derive` or `split`—then `release`, before restoring availability. Their contract below is **normative for the standard-library arena** until Spec 10 takes responsibility for it. It authorizes neither new permissions nor an additional access machine. Arena entries (Section 46) constitute the abstract state of this administration; the guard in Section 56 belongs to its consistency contract. The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here.

## 76. O17 — Creation of an Administered Arena

**Preconditions**

1. `storage` is an existing, usable place under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It may be local, static, allocated, or a block issued by a previous arena.
2. `internal` is explicitly named by the caller, exists, is active, has own mode `Modify`, and `ExercisableAt(s,internal,Modify)` holds.
3. `internal` is **held by a place**: that place is the arena value; `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)`.
4. **Unified administration guard (Section 56):** no **live** administrative abstraction, whether an arena or a library instance such as a handle pool, already uses this `internal` identity. The relevant registries of library administrations are consulted before registration. Two distinct identities may cover common leaves: this is not in itself grounds for rejection.
5. All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are already `Init`; construction does not initialize them implicitly.
6. Dependency, holder, storage, and administration relations respect, in the resulting state, `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, and `AnchorOrderHeld` over the whole kernel state, and the new entry satisfies `ArenaInv` (Section 55).

**`ok` effect:** A live entry `{storage, internal, available, issued}` is added; the initial `available` set represents the administered storage, and `issued` is initially empty. Registering the entry fabricates no place, access right, or `Init` state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

The identity of `internal`, not the index of `storage`, is the key to preventing duplication of live administrations. No global constraint requires footprints of live arenas to be pairwise disjoint.

## 77. O18 — Issuing an Arena Block

**Static preconditions**

1. The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active. `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value holding `internal` (Section 36). Mutation of metadata through `writeShared` alone does not satisfy this condition.
2. `region` belongs to the administered storage; `destination` is a usable **leaf** holding no active authority; the destination can legally receive the block value in mode `Modify`. The fact that `destination` is already `Init` is not in itself grounds for rejection, in accordance with O8.2.
   **Local self-blocking prevention: leaf `destination` is not in `region`, including when the region is declared available.** This condition is static and is checked before an availability `fail`.
3. Applicable **static** validity and non-escape restrictions for the destination are satisfied. The `AnchorOrder` check depending on the new anchor is performed on the **simulated resulting state**, after the availability check described in point 4; it cannot turn an unavailable issuance (`fail`) into `reject`.

**Availability and exercisability checks**

4. If static conditions hold but **at least one leaf of `region` does not belong to `available`**, the operation produces **`fail` and leaves the entire state unchanged**. The empty region is always available. An unavailable region does not permit a prior static rejection to be bypassed.
5. If the region is available, the effective mode of `internal` on that region must permit `Modify`; otherwise the outcome is `reject`.
6. The simulated result must satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` **in the resulting state**; moreover, **in that resulting state, `destination` must remain under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame**, in accordance with O8.5. Issuance into a value with a longer lifetime than a local anchor is not made valid merely by storing it in the caller.

**`ok` effect:** A block authority of fresh identity, derived from `internal` and of mode `Modify`, is issued for the region; it is held by `destination`, which receives the corresponding anchor. The leaves of the region leave `available`, and the issuance is added to `issued` with its authority. **Only leaf `destination` becomes `Init`**; no other leaf of the arena value changes initialization. Previous issuances remain intact and valid. Issuance does not automatically install anchors on third-party values: they must use their lawful dependency mechanisms.

**Outcomes:** `ok`, `fail` (region unavailable after static validation), `reject` (static rule, effective right, or anchoring not satisfied). The destination may be a leaf of the arena value itself: its initialization then constitutes **an explicit write to that destination**, not implicit initialization of the entire arena value's metadata.

## 78. O19 — Collective Arena Reset

**Preconditions**

1. The entry exists and is live. **`MetaRight(s,arena)` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value**, in accordance with Section 36. `writeShared` over metadata alone, even when legal, does not replace such exercise. `internal` and the arena's other restrictions remain valid.
2. **No active authority derived from `internal` covers a leaf of the administered storage.** A derived authority with an empty footprint does not, by itself, block `reset`.
3. No still-usable place depends, directly or transitively, on an anchor in the **strict origin subtree of `internal`** (`internal` itself is excluded) that covers a leaf of the administered storage. Under precondition 2 and invariant I3, this condition follows from the absence of active descendants covering the storage, and remains explicit in the abstraction contract. Validity obligations of other nested arenas remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** All **leaves** of the administered storage become available again, and the issuance list is cleared under the arena contract. No still-active derived authority covering those leaves may remain, by precondition 2; an empty-footprint derivative may remain active without designating any recycled leaf. **No leaf is made `Init` by `reset`**, including in the arena value. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Safe reuse after `reset` requires that previous issuances **covering recycled leaves**, and the dependencies on which their validity rests, have effectively ceased preventing their reuse. Any active empty-footprint derivatives cover none of those leaves. A historically issued region does not remain permanently unavailable solely for that reason.
