import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main

/-!
# Arenas: the reference library abstraction (Part XIV)

Arenas of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`, Part XIV (§76–§78), with §36, §46, §55,
§56, §58, §79, §86 and §88. An arena is a library abstraction (Part XIV): its entries live in a
library state separate from the kernel state `S₃` (§38, §46). `newArena` (O17) only registers an
entry; `issue` (O18) and `reset` (O19) are defined twice:

* as their contracts, clause by clause (§77, §78): `IssueC`, `ResetC`;
* as derived operations over the kernel steps (Part XIV): `issue` is its static checks, the
  availability `fail`, then `split` of `internal` on the region and `store` of the block into the
  destination (`IssueD`); `reset` is `derive` of `internal` at `Modify` over the whole storage,
  then `release`, then the explicit check of §78.3 (`ResetD`), which never rejects after an
  accepted `derive` on states satisfying I3 (`resetNoDeps_of_derive`).

On library-reachable states, `issue_as_kernel` and `reset_as_kernel` show that both definitions
have the same outcomes and the same arrival states, and `lReach_inv` that every live entry
satisfies `ArenaInv` (§55). Library reachability (`LReach`, `LReachNG`) uses the derived
operations, so its kernel states are kernel-reachable (`newArena_as_library`) and satisfy the
kernel invariant of §57 (`Access.reachable_kinv`).
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Arena

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Library state (§46) -/

/-- Arena entry (§46): administered storage, `internal` authority, available leaves and issued
regions with their block authorities. The sets of §46 are lists read by membership. -/
structure ArenaEntry where
  storage : Nat
  internal : Nat
  available : List Nat
  issued : List (List Nat × Nat)
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Library state (§46, §38): the kernel state `S₃` and, separately, the arena registry. -/
structure LState where
  kern : S3
  arenas : List ArenaEntry

/-- Initial library state (§47): the initial kernel state and an empty arena registry. -/
def LState.init (statics : Statics) : LState := ⟨S3.init statics, []⟩

/-- Live arena (§46): `internal` is active. -/
def Live (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Prop := s.Active E.internal

/-- Decidability of `Live` (§46). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Decidable (Live s E) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (s.Active _))

/-- Arena value (§46): the place holding `internal`. -/
def arenaValue (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Option Nat :=
  match s.A[E.internal]? with
  | some y => match y.holder with
    | .place v => some v
    | .frame _ => none
  | none => none

/-- `MetaRight(s, arena)` (§36, §77.1, §78.1): exercisable `Modify` over the arena value; there is
no `writeShared` branch. -/
def MetaRight (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Prop :=
  OptP (arenaValue s E) (fun v => HasRight s .modify v) False

/-- Decidability of `MetaRight` (§36). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Decidable (MetaRight s E) := by
  unfold MetaRight; infer_instance

/-- Available region (§46): each of its leaves belongs to `available`; the empty region is always
available. -/
def Avail (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) : Prop := ∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ E.available

/-- Decidability of `Avail` (§46). -/
instance (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) : Decidable (Avail E region) := by
  unfold Avail; infer_instance

/-! ## `ArenaInv` (§55) -/

/-! ## O17 `newArena` (§76) and the guard of §56 -/

/-- All leaves of the place holding an authority are `Init` (§76.5); vacuous for a frame. -/
def LeavesInit (s : S3) : Holder → Prop
  | .place v => ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P v, s.I l = .init
  | .frame _ => True

/-- Decidability of `LeavesInit` (§76.5). -/
instance (s : S3) (h : Holder) : Decidable (LeavesInit s h) := by
  cases h <;> unfold LeavesInit <;> infer_instance

/-- The unified administration guard (§56, §76.4) as a contract predicate: `internal` is absent
from every registry of live administrations. A registry is given by the `internal` identities of
its live administrations; `regs` lists all relevant registries. -/
def Guard56 (regs : List (List Nat)) (i : Nat) : Prop := ∀ R ∈ regs, i ∉ R

/-- Decidability of `Guard56` (§56). -/
instance (regs : List (List Nat)) (i : Nat) : Decidable (Guard56 regs i) := by
  unfold Guard56; infer_instance

/-- The arena registry as a registry of live administrations (§46, §56): the `internal`
identities of its live entries. -/
def liveInternals (s : S3) (arenas : List ArenaEntry) : List Nat :=
  (arenas.filter fun E => decide (s.Active E.internal)).map (·.internal)

/-- Preconditions of `newArena(storage, internal)` other than the guard (§76.1–§76.3, §76.5,
§76.6). §76.6 is read on the resulting state (v0.1 §76.6): its kernel component is `s`, since
`newArena` changes no kernel component (§76 `ok` effect, `newArena_kernel`), so `WF3`, `I1`,
`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are required of the whole kernel state `s`; the new entry is
the one `newArenaEff` registers, `available` holding the leaves of the storage and `issued`
empty, and it must satisfy `ArenaInv` (§55). -/
structure NewArenaBase (s : S3) (storage internal : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §76.1: `storage` is an existing, usable place. -/
  storageUsable : s.Usable storage
  /-- §76.1: `storage` is under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. -/
  storageRight : HasRight s .modify storage
  /-- §76.2: `internal` exists, is active and has own mode `Modify`. -/
  internalAuth : OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.mode = .modify) False
  /-- §76.2: `ExercisableAt(s, internal, Modify)`. -/
  exercisable : s.ExercisableAt internal .modify
  /-- §76.3: `internal` is held by a place, the arena value. -/
  heldByPlace : OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => y.holder.isPlace = true) False
  /-- §76.3: `footprint(internal) ⊆ footprint(storage)`. -/
  fpSub : ∀ l ∈ s.afp internal, l ∈ footprint s.P storage
  /-- §76.3: `footprint(storage) ⊆ footprint(internal)`. -/
  fpSup : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, l ∈ s.afp internal
  /-- §76.5: all leaves of the arena value are already `Init`. -/
  valueInit : OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => LeavesInit s y.holder) True
  /-- §76.6: `WF3` (§49) over the whole kernel state of the resulting state. -/
  wf3 : WF3 s
  /-- §76.6: `I1` (§50) over the whole kernel state of the resulting state. -/
  i1 : I1 s
  /-- §76.6: `AnchorOrder` (§44) over the whole kernel state of the resulting state. -/
  anchorOrder : AnchorOrder s
  /-- §76.6: `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44) over the whole kernel state of the resulting state. -/
  anchorOrderHeld : AnchorOrderHeld s
  /-- §76.6: the new entry satisfies `ArenaInv` (§55). -/
  arenaInv : ArenaInv s ⟨storage, internal, footprint s.P storage, []⟩

/-- Decidability of `NewArenaBase` (§76). -/
instance (s : S3) (storage internal : Nat) : Decidable (NewArenaBase s storage internal) :=
  decidable_of_iff (s.Usable storage ∧ HasRight s .modify storage ∧
    OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.mode = .modify) False ∧
    s.ExercisableAt internal .modify ∧
    OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => y.holder.isPlace = true) False ∧
    (∀ l ∈ s.afp internal, l ∈ footprint s.P storage) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, l ∈ s.afp internal) ∧
    OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => LeavesInit s y.holder) True ∧
    WF3 s ∧ I1 s ∧ AnchorOrder s ∧ AnchorOrderHeld s ∧
    ArenaInv s ⟨storage, internal, footprint s.P storage, []⟩)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l, m, n⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l, m, n⟩,
     fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l, m, n⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l, m, n⟩⟩

/-- Preconditions of `newArena(storage, internal)` (§76): those of `NewArenaBase` and the guard of
§76.4 over the arena registry and the other registries `others` (§56). -/
structure NewArenaPre (s : S3) (arenas : List ArenaEntry) (others : List (List Nat))
    (storage internal : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §76.1–§76.3, §76.5. -/
  base : NewArenaBase s storage internal
  /-- §76.4, §56: no live administration of any relevant registry uses `internal`. -/
  guard : Guard56 (liveInternals s arenas :: others) internal

/-- Decidability of `NewArenaPre` (§76). -/
instance (s : S3) (arenas : List ArenaEntry) (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) :
    Decidable (NewArenaPre s arenas others storage internal) :=
  decidable_of_iff (NewArenaBase s storage internal ∧
    Guard56 (liveInternals s arenas :: others) internal)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩, fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩⟩

/-- Effect of `newArena` (§76, `ok` effect): a live entry is added, `available` holding the leaves
of the storage and `issued` empty; the kernel state is unchanged. -/
def newArenaEff (L : LState) (storage internal : Nat) : LState :=
  { L with arenas := L.arenas ++ [⟨storage, internal, footprint L.kern.P storage, []⟩] }

/-- `newArena` as a relation (§76, §58): `ok` or `reject`; `others` are the other registries of
live administrations consulted by the guard (§56). -/
def NewArenaStep (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) (L : LState) :
    Outcome3 LState → Prop :=
  Guarded (NewArenaPre L.kern L.arenas others storage internal) (newArenaEff L storage internal)

/-! ## O18 `issue` (§77) -/

/-- Static preconditions of `issue(arena, region, destination)` (§77.1, §77.2). The static
restrictions of §77.3 are given no list by the text and are not represented. -/
structure IssueStatic (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §77.1: the entry is live; `internal` is active. -/
  live : s.Active E.internal
  /-- §77.1: `MetaRight`, exercisable `Modify` over the arena value (§36). -/
  metaRight : MetaRight s E
  /-- §77.2: `region` belongs to the administered storage. -/
  regionIn : ∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ footprint s.P E.storage
  /-- §77.2: `destination` is usable. -/
  dstUsable : s.Usable dst
  /-- §77.2: `destination` is a leaf. -/
  dstLeaf : isLeaf s.P dst
  /-- §77.2: `destination` holds no active authority. -/
  dstFree : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
    OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True
  /-- §77.2: `destination` can legally receive the block value in mode `Modify`. -/
  dstRight : HasRight s .modify dst
  /-- §77.2: local self-blocking prevention, `destination` is not in `region`. -/
  dstNotIn : dst ∉ region

/-- Decidability of `IssueStatic` (§77). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (IssueStatic s E region dst) :=
  decidable_of_iff (s.Active E.internal ∧ MetaRight s E ∧
    (∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ footprint s.P E.storage) ∧ s.Usable dst ∧ isLeaf s.P dst ∧
    (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
      OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True) ∧
    HasRight s .modify dst ∧ dst ∉ region)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h⟩,
     fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h⟩⟩

/-- §77.5: the effective mode of `internal` permits `Modify` on every leaf of the region. -/
def IssueRight (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ l ∈ region, Allows (effective s E.internal l) .modify

/-- Decidability of `IssueRight` (§77.5). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) : Decidable (IssueRight s E region) := by
  unfold IssueRight; infer_instance

/-- Kernel part of the effect of `issue` (§77, `ok` effect): a block authority of fresh identity
`|A|`, derived from `internal`, of mode `Modify`, on the region, held by `destination`, which
receives the corresponding anchor; only leaf `destination` becomes `Init`. -/
def issueKEff (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s with
    A := s.A ++ [⟨.modify, some E.internal, region, .place dst, true⟩]
    D := fun q => if q = dst then s.D dst ++ [s.A.length] else s.D q
    I := fun l => if l = dst then .init else s.I l }

/-- Metadata part of the effect of `issue` (§77, `ok` effect; §46): the leaves of the region leave
`available`; the issuance joins `issued` with its authority. -/
def issueMeta (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) : ArenaEntry :=
  { E with
    available := E.available.filter fun l => decide (l ∉ region)
    issued := (region, s.A.length) :: E.issued }

/-- Checks of `issue` on the simulated resulting state (§77.3, §77.6). -/
structure IssueArrival (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §77.3: `AnchorOrder` for the new anchor of `destination`, in the resulting state. -/
  anchorOrder : EffAnchorOK (issueKEff s E region dst) s.A.length
    ((issueKEff s E region dst).pframe dst)
  /-- §77.6: `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state. -/
  anchorOrderHeld : AnchorOrderHeld (issueKEff s E region dst)
  /-- §77.6, O8.5: `destination` remains under exercisable `Modify` in the resulting state. -/
  keepsDst : HasRight (issueKEff s E region dst) .modify dst

/-- Decidability of `IssueArrival` (§77). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :

12:6. DataStack (contract below, identifier DS-v1). Marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it; push and grow use the derived issue; grow is in place only (same base, extension into the space directly after the block, fail otherwise). Theorems: rewind_rejects_live_above, mark_no_aba (for every removed mark), rewind_keeps_older_marks, grow_same_base, grow_keeps_prefix_init, grow_keeps_prefix_bytes through the refinement.

- Readings: valid means "exists" (current, `Access.I2`) or "active".
- Program W2 (`R/report-check/kd_Readings.lean`:17-26, re-checked at HEAD): `a := derive(root x, [x], Modify)`, `store(a, r)`, `b := derive(a, [x], Observe)`, `endUse(r)`. `endUse` is `ok` and leaves `b` active with an inactive origin. I2 holds under "exists" and fails under "active". The draft's ancestor disjunct of §69.2, dropped by policy, would reject the `endUse`.

**Q10. §61.4 (B38).**
- Passage: "Creation of the derivatives respects origins, conservation I1/I2, and validity obligations." Note to §61: "without `DDSound`, an accepted `split` may violate I1".
- Readings: (a) not a precondition (current); (b) a precondition.
- Program: `split` under an unsound `DeclaredDisjoint`. It is `ok` under (a) and `reject` under (b) (`Access.split_unsound_without_DD`, DeriveSplitRelease.lean:762).

**Q11. DataStack readings (contract DS-v1, non-normative; B29, B30).**
- Passages: "rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark", "push and grow use the derived issue", "grow is in place only (same base, extension into the space directly after the block, fail otherwise)".
- (a) DS-R7: `push` without room. `fail` (current) or `reject` (§77.2 static). Program `Corpus.DataStack.DS05`.
- (b) DS-R5: `grow` of a `b` that is no block. `reject` (current) or `fail`. Program `Corpus.DataStack.DS03`, conjunct `GrowStep K0 0 6 1 ds03 .reject`.
- (c) DS-R9: §76.5 applies to `newStack`. `Witness.reading_newStack` (DataStack.lean:1314): `reject` here, `ok` without §76.5.
- (d) DS-R10: `mark` needs no right. `Witness.reading_mark` (:1251): `ok` here, `reject` under §36 ¶1.
- (e) DS-R11: the `grow` destination is the recorded `Blk.dst`. `Witness.reading_grow_dst` (:1280): the arrival holder is place 4 here and place 5 under the alternative.
- (f) DS-R2: the dead or foreign mark gives `fail` before §36 (current), or the right is checked first (`reject`). Program: a callee with no right rewinds to a removed mark (`R/readings/datastack.md` DS-R2, `Witness.reading_order`).
- (g) DS-R12 and DS-R13, the reasons for which `rewind` rejects: Q27 and Q28.

**Q12. HandlePool D.3: `freeSlot` of a free slot whose identity and generation match (B21).**
- Passage: "un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité".
- Readings: `fail` (H-R2, current) or `reject`.
- Program: `Corpus.Lib.pool_free_entry_handle` (Lib.lean:313).

**Q13. §71.2 vs §36 (B39).**
- Passages: §71.2, "updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata". §36, "Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant the right to create, recycle, or terminate exclusive authority over the administered storage".
- Program: a provider leaf that is `SharedMutable`, with an `Observe` derivative held by the frame and no `Modify`. `alloc` is `ok` under §71.2 (current `AllocStatic.providerRight`, Ops.lean:872) and forbidden under §36.
- Readings: (a) strict literal: an authority held by the surviving `place` blocks `endUse`; (b) `place`, whose value dies, counts among the dying places (current: `Access.EndUseAccessOK`, Ops.lean:709, exempts every authority held within `place`). The mixed reading actually used is recorded in neither `R/readings/kernel-defs.md` B#28 nor B#29.
- Program: `R/report-check/records/V_r0.lean`:54-71, from the statics of `Access.Examples`: `alloc` (provider 0, owner 1) makes place 3; `derive(3, [3], Modify)` gives authority 4; `store(4, 0)`; `transfer(0, 1)`; then `endUse(1)` while authority 4 is held by place 1, which survives. It is `ok` under (b) (`EndUsePre K0 sd 1`) and `reject` under (a) (`EndUseAccessOK sd 1 4 ∧ ¬ StrictAccessOK sd 1 4`).

**Q26. §60.1 "its origin chain and anchors are valid", read through §44 (round 0, ops-a R1; linked to Q9).**
- Passage: §60.1. §44 gives "valid" a meaning: an anchor is valid while the authority it names is active. `R/readings/kernel-defs.md` SP-A5 and the policy record the clause as having no checkable content; round 0 (ops-a R1) found that record misdescribed.
- Readings: valid means "exists" (the clause is then redundant with WF3.5, and omitting it, as the model does, changes nothing) or "active" (as in Q9).
- Program: `R/report-check/records/r60.lean`: after the W2 run of Q9, `derive(3, [0], Observe)`, whose origin 2 is inactive. It is `ok` under "exists" (current, `R60.r60`) and `reject` under "active".

**Q27. DS-v1 `rewind`: does §36 add a reason to reject? (DS-R12; contract DS-v1, non-normative; B47 note in section 1).**
- Passages: DS-v1, "rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it". It names one reason to reject. §36, "For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**", and "These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel".
- Readings: (a) §36 applies, so `rewind` also rejects without `AdminRight` (current). On library-reachable states (`DReach`) and for an existing stack, this is the only reason outside DS-v1's list (`Lib.DataStack.rewind_ok_iff`, DataStack.lean:719). That `ok` is then the only outcome is not stated in the module; it follows from `Guarded.det` (`Access.Guarded.det`, MemoryModel/Access/Lemmas.lean:207; scratch proof `R/../records-chk/okonly.lean`, `rewind_only_ok`). (b) DS-v1's list is exhaustive, so `rewind` is `ok` whenever the mark is live and no active authority derived from `internal` covers a cell above it.
- Program: `Lib.DataStack.Witness.reading_rewind_right` (:1338), state `d16` (:1329). After the rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩` and the program's `release(5)`, a callee frame with no parameter or local is entered. Mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0, and no active authority derived from `internal` 4 covers cell 2, the cell above it. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` under (a) and `ok` under (b). The kernel sequence cannot realize (b) there: `split` of `internal` also rejects, because `internal` is not exercisable at `Modify` (§61.1).
- Scope: existing stacks. A stack index with no stack gives `reject` through `RewindStep.noStack` (DataStack.lean:218), a further reason outside DS-v1's list (DS-R3, `R/final5/nostack.lean`; submitted with Q23).

**Q28. DS-v1 `rewind` on a live mark of a dead stack (DS-R13; contract DS-v1, non-normative; narrow check ds4-3).**
- Passages: DS-v1, "the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark". DS-v1 does not speak of a dead stack. §46, "The arena is **live** if `internal` is active", which `Lib.DataStack.AdminRight` (DataStack.lean:108) reads for a stack. §77.1, "The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active". §61.1, "`source` is active and exercisable by the current frame".
- Readings:
  - (a) `reject` (current; forced by the §61.1 check of the derived reset; also by the `Active internal` conjunct of `AdminRight`, constructor `RewindStep.static`);
  - (b) DS-v1's list is exhaustive (Q27 (b)): `ok`;
  - (c) a mark of a dead stack is a dead mark: `fail` (under the DS-R2 order the mark is checked first).
  - The only alternatives that change the verdict are (c) `fail` and (b) `ok`, and (b) is possible only if `rewind` skips the derived reset. Whether the liveness of the stack is part of the §36 check does not change the verdict.
- Program: `R/final5/d17.lean`, re-elaborated against HEAD. `d17` is `d11` (after the rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩` and the program's `release(5)`) followed by the program's `release(4)` of `internal` 4. Mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0, no active authority derived from `internal` covers cell 2, `MetaRight` still holds and `internal` is inactive (`d17_facts`). `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` and nothing else under (a) (`d17_only_reject`), `ok` under (b) and `fail` under (c). The kernel sequence cannot realize (b): in `d17`, `split` of `internal` rejects because `internal` is inactive (§61.1; `SplitPre.active`, the same test as the first conjunct of `AdminRight`). Without that conjunct the outcome stays `reject` through `RewindStep.split` (`R/../records-chk/q28split.lean`, `d17_split_rejects`: `¬ Active`, `¬ SplitPre` and `SplitStep … .reject` on `d17`).
- `d16` of Q27 does not exercise this case: there `internal` is active and only `MetaRight` fails.

import Ern.Lib.DataStack

open Ern.MemoryModel Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena Ern.Lib.DataStack
open Ern.Lib.DataStack.Witness Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Examples

def d17 : DState := ⟨releaseEff d11.kern 4, d11.stacks, d11.fresh⟩

theorem d17_facts :
    DReach K0 wst d17 ∧ d17.stacks[0]? = some st9 ∧ LiveMark 0 st9 m0 ∧
    ¬ d17.kern.Active st9.internal ∧ MetaRight d17.kern st9.entry ∧
    (∀ x ∈ List.range d17.kern.A.length, OptP (d17.kern.A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true →
      st9.internal ∈ d17.kern.ancs x → ∀ l ∈ above st9 m0, l ∉ y.footprint) True) ∧
    ¬ AdminRight d17.kern st9 ∧ RewindStep K0 0 m0 d17 .reject := by
  have r11 : DReach K0 wst d11 := .step d9_reach (.kernel (.release (.ok (by decide))))
  have r17 : DReach K0 wst d17 := .step r11 (.kernel (.release (.ok (by decide))))
  exact ⟨r17, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide,
    .static (st := st9) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)⟩

-- the outcome is only reject: no fail, no ok
theorem d17_only_reject : ∀ o, RewindStep K0 0 m0 d17 o → o = .reject := by
  intro o h
  cases h with
  | noStack h => rfl
  | dead h hm => exact absurd (by decide : LiveMark 0 st9 m0) (by
      have : d17.stacks[0]? = some st9 := by decide
      rw [this] at h; cases h; exact hm)
  | static => rfl
  | split => rfl
  | release => rfl
  | ok h hm ha => exact absurd ha (by
      have : d17.stacks[0]? = some st9 := by decide
      rw [this] at h; cases h; decide)

-- d16: the DS-R12 witness has a live stack
example : d16.kern.Active st9.internal ∧ ¬ MetaRight d16.kern st9.entry := by decide
example : above st9 m0 = [2] := by decide

#print axioms d17_facts
#print axioms d17_only_reject
-----
import Ern.Lib.DataStack
open Ern.MemoryModel Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena Ern.Lib.DataStack Ern.Lib.DataStack.Witness

-- initial (reachable) state: no stack; rewind 0 m0 rejects via noStack, never ok, never fail
example : DReach Examples.K0 wst d0 ∧ RewindStep Examples.K0 0 m0 d0 .reject ∧
    (¬ ∃ D', RewindStep Examples.K0 0 m0 d0 (.ok D')) ∧ ¬ RewindStep Examples.K0 0 m0 d0 .fail := by
  have h0 : d0.stacks[0]? = none := by decide
  refine ⟨.init, .noStack h0, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rintro ⟨D', h⟩; cases h <;> simp_all
  · intro h; cases h <;> simp_all
-- the only reject constructor applicable is noStack (no stack value)
example : d0.stacks = [] := rfl

/-! ## Transport of `EntryInv` (§55) -/

/-- `s'` keeps the authorities of `s` (§42, §58): each keeps its mode and footprint, becomes
active only if it was, stays held by a place if it was, and keeps an origin `o` below it that is
active in `s'`. -/
def AKeep (s s' : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ j y, s.A[j]? = some y → ∃ y', s'.A[j]? = some y' ∧ y'.mode = y.mode ∧
    y'.footprint = y.footprint ∧ (y'.active = true → y.active = true) ∧
    (y'.holder.isPlace = false → y.holder.isPlace = false) ∧
    ∀ o, y.origin = some o → o < j → s'.Active o → y'.origin = some o

/-- Authorities are never reactivated (§42, §58). -/
theorem AKeep.active_back {s s' : S3} (h : AKeep s s') {x : Nat} (hx : s'.Active x)
    (hlt : x < s.A.length) : s.Active x := by
  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ : ∃ y, s.A[x]? = some y := ⟨_, List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.2 ⟨hlt, rfl⟩⟩
  obtain ⟨y', hy', -, -, ha, -⟩ := h x y hy
  obtain ⟨z, hz, za⟩ := hx
  rw [hy'] at hz; cases hz; exact ⟨y, hy, ha za⟩

/-- Authorities are never removed (§42). -/
theorem AKeep.lt {s s' : S3} (h : AKeep s s') {x : Nat} (hlt : x < s.A.length) :
    x < s'.A.length := by
  obtain ⟨y', hy', -⟩ := h x _ (List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.2 ⟨hlt, rfl⟩)
  exact lt_of_getElem? hy'

/-- `AKeep` composes (§42). -/
theorem AKeep.trans {s s' s'' : S3} (h : AKeep s s') (h' : AKeep s' s'') : AKeep s s'' := by
  intro j y hy
  obtain ⟨y', hy', m, f, a, p, o⟩ := h j y hy
  obtain ⟨y'', hy'', m', f', a', p', o'⟩ := h' j y' hy'
  refine ⟨y'', hy'', m'.trans m, f'.trans f, fun h => a (a' h), fun h => p (p' h),
    fun x hx hxj hxa => o' x (o x hx hxj ?_) hxj hxa⟩
  obtain ⟨z, hz, za⟩ := hxa
  obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ : ∃ w, s'.A[x]? = some w := by
    obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀⟩ : ∃ y₀, s.A[x]? = some y₀ :=
      ⟨_, List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.2 ⟨Nat.lt_trans hxj (lt_of_getElem? hy), rfl⟩⟩
    obtain ⟨w, hw, -⟩ := h x y₀ hy₀; exact ⟨w, hw⟩
  obtain ⟨z', hz', -, -, ha, -⟩ := h' x w hw
  rw [hz] at hz'; cases hz'; exact ⟨w, hw, ha za⟩

/-- Unchanged authorities (§42). -/
theorem akeep_of_eq {s s' : S3} (hA : s'.A = s.A) : AKeep s s' := by
  intro j y hy
  refine ⟨y, by rw [hA]; exact hy, rfl, rfl, id, id, fun o ho _ _ => ho⟩

/-- Appended authorities (§60, §61, §71, §77, §78). -/
theorem akeep_append {s s' : S3} {l : List Authority} (hA : s'.A = s.A ++ l) : AKeep s s' := by
  intro j y hy
  refine ⟨y, by rw [hA, List.getElem?_append_left (lt_of_getElem? hy)]; exact hy, rfl, rfl, id,
    id, fun o ho _ _ => ho⟩

/-- Authorities mapped by a function keeping mode, footprint, origin and place holders, and
activating nothing (§62, §63, §69, §70). -/
theorem akeep_map {s s' : S3} {f : Authority → Authority} (hA : s'.A = s.A.map f)
    (hf : ∀ y, (f y).mode = y.mode ∧ (f y).footprint = y.footprint ∧
      ((f y).active = true → y.active = true) ∧
      ((f y).holder.isPlace = false → y.holder.isPlace = false) ∧ (f y).origin = y.origin) :
    AKeep s s' := by
  intro j y hy
  obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4, h5⟩ := hf y
  exact ⟨f y, by rw [hA, List.getElem?_map, hy]; rfl, h1, h2, h3, h4, fun o ho _ _ => h5 ▸ ho⟩

/-- One authority replaced by a record with the same mode, footprint and origin, active only if
it was, held by a place if it was (§62, §65). -/
theorem akeep_set {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} {x x' : Authority} (hx : s.A[a]? = some x)
    (hA : s'.A = s.A.set a x') (hm : x'.mode = x.mode) (hf : x'.footprint = x.footprint)
    (ha : x'.active = true → x.active = true)
    (hp : x'.holder.isPlace = false → x.holder.isPlace = false) (ho : x'.origin = x.origin) :
    AKeep s s' := by
  intro j y hy
  by_cases hj : a = j
  · subst hj; rw [hx] at hy; cases hy

def opEff : Machine.Op Ty → Machine.State → Machine.State
  | .read _ _, s => s
  | .write ac _ w, s => s.write ac w
  | .dealloc id _, s => s.dealloc id
  | .alloc sp b sz al fa, s => s.alloc sp b sz al fa

/-- State after a sequence of `ok` raw operations (§20.3 ¶3). -/
def run : Machine.State → List (Machine.Op Ty) → Machine.State
  | s, [] => s
  | s, o :: os => run (opEff o s) os

/-- `p s o` holds for each operation `o` of the sequence in the state where it runs (§20.3). -/
def Along (p : Machine.State → Machine.Op Ty → Prop) :
    Machine.State → List (Machine.Op Ty) → Prop
  | _, [] => True
  | s, o :: os => p s o ∧ Along p (opEff o s) os

/-- Decidability of `Along` for a decidable property (§20.3 ¶3). -/
instance decAlong (p : Machine.State → Machine.Op Ty → Prop) [h : ∀ s o, Decidable (p s o)] :
    (s : Machine.State) → (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) → Decidable (Along p s os)
  | _, [] => isTrue trivial

/-! ## R2: safe writes (§82.2, §67, §68, §16) -/

/-- The writes realizing `write(access, ls)` and `writeShared(access, ls)` (§82.2, §67, §68): one
raw write per leaf, of the range of the leaf, at the type `ty l`, of the representation `w l`
supplied by the program (§10 ¶4, §16 ¶2). -/
def writeOps {Ty : Type} (s2 : Machine.State) (L : Layout) (ty : Nat → Ty)
    (w : Nat → Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) (ls : List Nat) : List (Machine.Op Ty) :=
  ls.map fun l => .write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (ty l) (w l)

/-- The writes of the ranges of leaves whose allocations are live and contain them are `ok` under
their parametric obligations (§16, §82.2), and afterwards every written range is initialized
(§16 ¶2). -/
theorem writes_ok {Ty : Type} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {L : Layout} {ty : Nat → Ty}
    {w : Nat → Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} :
    ∀ (ls : List Nat) (s2 : Machine.State), Machine.WF s2 →
      (∀ l ∈ ls, AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun a => a.live = true ∧ (L l).off + (L l).len ≤ a.size) →
      OblAlong ObR ObW s2 (writeOps s2 L ty w ls) →
      Along (OkAt C ObR ObW) s2 (writeOps s2 L ty w ls) ∧
        ∀ l ∈ ls, AllocP (run s2 (writeOps s2 L ty w ls)) (L l).alloc
          fun a => a.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len
  | [], _, _, _, _ => ⟨trivial, fun _ h => nomatch h⟩
  | l :: ls, s2, hwf, hls, hob => by
    obtain ⟨al, hal, hlive, hsz⟩ := hls l (List.mem_cons_self ..)
    have hex : AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun _ => True := ⟨al, hal, trivial⟩
    have hd₁ : Dom s2 (s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (w l)) :=
      dom_opEff (Ty := Ty) hwf (.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (ty l) (w l))
    have hwf₁ : Machine.WF (s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (w l)) :=
      Machine.write_wf hwf _ _
    have hops : writeOps (s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (w l)) L ty w ls =
  | [] => baseOf s2 (anchorAlloc L s3 a)

/-- The raw operation realizing `store(authority, target)` (§82.2, §82.3, §65): one write into the
range of the leaf `target` of the reference to the region of the authority, with the address of
`ptrAddr` and the provenance of the allocation of its effective anchor (§82.2). -/
def storeOps {Ty : Type} (pe : PtrEnc) (s2 : Machine.State) (L : Layout) (ty : Nat → Ty) (s3 : S3)
    (a p : Nat) : List (Machine.Op Ty) :=
  writeOps s2 L ty (fun _ => pe.enc (ptrAddr s2 L s3 a) (some (anchorAlloc L s3 a))) [p]

/-- The target of an `ok` `store` is a leaf of a usable place (§65.2). -/
theorem store_target {s3 : S3} {a p : Nat} (hpre : StorePre s3 a p) : LeafOfUsable s3 p :=
      (∀ l ∈ s3.afp a, (L l).alloc = anchorAlloc L s3 a ∧
        AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun al => al.live = true ∧ (L l).off + (L l).len ≤ al.size) ∧
      ((∀ l ∈ s3.afp a, (L l).len = 0) → ad = baseOf s2 (anchorAlloc L s3 a)) ∧
      ((∃ l ∈ s3.afp a, 0 < (L l).len) → ∃ l ∈ s3.afp a, 0 < (L l).len ∧ ad = leafAddr s2 L l ∧
        ∀ l' ∈ s3.afp a, 0 < (L l').len → ad ≤ leafAddr s2 L l') := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, -⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  obtain ⟨hpP, hpf, hpu⟩ := leaf_of_leafOfUsable hw (store_target hpre)
  obtain ⟨pa, hpa, -⟩ := hR.leaf_live hw hpP hpf hpu
  have hrun : run s2 (storeOps (Ty := Ty) pe s2 L ty s3 a p) =
      s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write p) (pe.enc ad (some (anchorAlloc L s3 a))) := by
    simp only [storeOps, had, writeOps, List.map_cons, List.map_nil, run, opEff]
  have hbytes : ∀ i, i < (L p).len →
      bytesOf (run s2 (storeOps (Ty := Ty) pe s2 L ty s3 a p)) L p i =
      pe.enc ad (some (anchorAlloc L s3 a)) i := fun i hi => by
    rw [hrun]; exact bytesOf_write ⟨pa, hpa, trivial⟩ hi
  have hy : ∃ y, s3.A[a]? = some y ∧ y.active = true := by
def opsOf {Ty : Type} (π : Params Ty) : KOp → S3 → Machine.State → List (Machine.Op Ty)
  | .transfer src dst, s3, s2 => transferOps π.L π.ty s2 s3 src dst
  | .enter _ ls, s3, s2 => allocOps π.pl π.geom π.rtok s3.P.length s2 (rootIdx ls.toShape)
  | .exit, s3, _ => exitOps π.L π.rtok s3
  | .read _ ls, _, s2 => readOps s2 π.L π.ty ls

/-! ## O13 `free` (§70) -/

/-- The holder is a place (§70.1). -/
def Holder.isPlace : Holder → Bool
  | .place _ => true
  | .frame _ => false

/-- `OwnedRoot` (§70.1): a place with no structural parent, owned by a place. -/
def OwnedRoot (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
    obtain ⟨x, hx, hlx⟩ := mem_of_allows (hall l hl)
    rw [addAuth_self] at hx; cases hx
    exact absurd hlx (hout l hl)

/-- The effect of `store` on an existing authority (§65, `ok` effect). -/
theorem storeEff_eq {s : S3} {a p : Nat} {y : Authority} (hy : s.A[a]? = some y) :
    storeEff s a p = { s with
      A := s.A.set a { y with holder := .place p }
      D := fun q => if q = p then s.D p ++ [a] else s.D q
      I := fun l => if l = p then .init else s.I l } := by
  simp [storeEff, hy]

/-- `store` changes holders only (§65, `ok` effect). -/
theorem store_skel (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : SameSkel s (storeEff s a p) := by
  unfold storeEff; split
  · rename_i y hy

/-- The block added by `split` of `internal` on the region (§61, `ok` effect). -/
theorem split_block (s : S3) (src : Nat) (region : List Nat) :
    (splitEff s src [region]).A[s.A.length]? =
      some ⟨.modify, some src, region, .frame s.top, true⟩ := by
  simp [splitEff]

/-- The kernel part of the effect of `issue` is the arrival state of `split` of `internal` on the
region followed by `store` of the block into the destination (Part XIV, §77): literal
equality. -/
theorem issueKEff_eq (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
    issueKEff s E region dst = storeEff (splitEff s E.internal [region]) s.A.length dst := by
  rw [storeEff_eq (split_block s E.internal region)]

abstraction adds no rights to the kernel (§36).

/-- The grown block (DS-v1, non-normative: same base, `extra` more cells, new authority `a`, same
destination; an issuance of §46). -/
def growBlk (x : Blk) (extra a : Nat) : Blk := ⟨x.base, x.size + extra, a, x.dst⟩

/-- Metadata after `grow` (DS-v1, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §77 on §46 metadata): the
top rises by `extra`; the block is replaced by the grown block. -/
def growMeta (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra a : Nat) : Stack :=
  { st with
    top := st.top + extra
    blocks := st.blocks.map fun y => if y.auth = x.auth then growBlk x extra a else y }

/-- `grow(j, b, extra)` (DS-v1, non-normative: in place only, using the derived `issue`): `reject`
when `b` is not a block of the stack or `extra` is zero (reading recorded); `release` of `b` (O3);
then the derived `issue` of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`) of the region of the same base and of size
`size + extra` into the recorded destination, on the released state: its static checks
(`IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2), `fail`, the state unchanged, unless the extension is in place
(DS-v1 "fail otherwise", availability §77.4), `split` of `internal` (O2) and `store` of the new
block (O8). -/

  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | noBlock {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = none →
      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | noExtra {st : Stack} {x : Blk} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x → extra = 0 →
      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | release {st : Stack} {x : Blk} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x → 0 < extra →
      ReleaseStep b D.kern .reject → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
  | static {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
      ¬ IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst →

/-- Metadata after `push` (DS-v2, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §77 on §46 metadata): the
cells leave the available part (the top rises by `size`), the block is recorded. -/
def pushMeta (st : Stack) (size a dst : Nat) : Stack :=
  { st with top := st.top + size, blocks := st.blocks ++ [⟨st.top, size, a, dst⟩] }

/-- `push(j, size, dst)` (DS-v2, non-normative: "push uses the derived issue"): the derived `issue`
of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`) of the `size` cells at the top into `dst`, on the stack seen as an
entry: its static checks (`IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2, with `MetaRight` of §36), then `fail`, the
state unchanged, when fewer than `size` cells are left (availability, §77.4; reading recorded),
then `split` of `internal` on the cells (O2) and `store` of the block, of fresh identity `|A|`, into
`dst` (O8). -/
inductive PushStep (k : K) (j size dst : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
  | static {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
      ¬ IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
  | fail {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
    fun j hj hn => ?_, fun q _ _ hx => absurd (hb q _ hx) (Nat.lt_irrefl _)⟩
  have := chain_lt hn
  have := List.mem_range.1 hj; simp [splitEff] at this; omega

/-- `rewind_ok_iff` (DS-v2, non-normative: "rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an
active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to
available"; §36; §61.1, §61.3, §62 through Part XIV). On a library-reachable state (`DReach`, a
state invariant), for an existing stack, `rewind m` is `ok` exactly when `m` is a live mark of the
stack (DS-v2), the administrative right of §36 holds (`AdminRight`), and no active authority
derived from `internal` covers a cell above `m` (DS-v2). The model has no explicit check of the
last condition: it is the effective `Modify` of `internal` required by `split` (§61.1, with the
effective mode of §43). The other checks of `split` and `release` never reject there: `internal`
has own mode `Modify` and covers the cells (`DReach.stackShape`, §76.2, §76.3), and anchors name
existing authorities (`dBound_of_reachable`). DS-v2 does not list §36: on the reachable state of
`Witness.reading_rewind_right` every DS-v2 condition for success holds and §36 rejects (the §61.1
check of `split` fails there too). -/
theorem rewind_ok_iff {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (hr : DReach k statics D)
    {j : Nat} {st : Stack} (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) {m : Mark} :
    (∃ D', RewindStep k j m D (.ok D')) ↔
      LiveMark D.kern j st m ∧ AdminRight D.kern st ∧
        ∀ (x l : Nat) (y : Authority), D.kern.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true →
instance (s : S3) (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Decidable (LiveMark s j st m) := by
  unfold LiveMark; infer_instance

/-- The administrative right of §36 for a stack (DS-v2, non-normative, with §36 and §46 read for a
stack): the stack is live (`internal` is active) and `MetaRight`, `Modify` exercisable on the stack
value, the place holding `internal`. -/
def AdminRight (s : S3) (st : Stack) : Prop := s.Active st.internal ∧ MetaRight s st.entry

/-- Decidability of `AdminRight` (§36; DS-v2). -/

/-! ## Library runs (DS-v2; §36, §56, §57) -/

/-- One `ok` step of the stack library (DS-v2, non-normative): a kernel step O1–O16 of
non-administrative code, the registry unchanged; `newStack` with the guard of §56 against the other
registries `others`; `push`, `mark`, `rewind`, `grow`. -/
inductive DStep (k : K) : DState → DState → Prop where
  | kernel {D : DState} {s' : S3} : KStep k D.kern s' → DStep k D ⟨s', D.stacks, D.fresh⟩
  | newStack {D D' : DState} {others : List (List Nat)} {storage i : Nat} :
      NewStackStep others storage i D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
  | push {D D' : DState} {j size dst : Nat} : PushStep k j size dst D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
  | mark {D D' : DState} {j : Nat} : MarkStep j D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
  | rewind {D D' : DState} {j : Nat} {m : Mark} : RewindStep k j m D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
  | grow {D D' : DState} {j b extra : Nat} : GrowStep k j b extra D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'

/-- States reachable from the initial state by library steps (DS-v2, non-normative; §47). -/
inductive DReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : DState → Prop where
  | init : DReach k statics (DState.init statics)
  | step {D D' : DState} : DReach k statics D → DStep k D D' → DReach k statics D'

/-- Finite sequences of library steps (DS-v2, non-normative; §58 `ok` transitions). -/
inductive DRun (k : K) : DState → DState → Prop where
  | refl (D : DState) : DRun k D D
  | tail {D D' D'' : DState} : DRun k D D' → DStep k D' D'' → DRun k D D''

/-- The kernel part of a library step is reached by kernel steps (§36: the abstraction adds no
rights to the kernel; Part XIV: `issue` is `split` then `store`, the reset part of `rewind` is
`split` then `release`; DS-v2). -/
theorem DStep.reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D D' : DState}
    (hr : Reachable k statics D.kern) (h : DStep k D D') : Reachable k statics D'.kern := by

/-! ## `mark` (DS-v2) -/

/-- Metadata after `mark` (DS-v2, non-normative; library metadata, §36, §38): a mark naming stack
`j`, with the fresh identifier `fresh` and the current top, is appended to the live marks. -/
def markMeta (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (fresh : Nat) : Stack :=
  { st with marks := st.marks ++ [⟨j, fresh, st.top⟩] }

/-- `mark(j)` (DS-v2, non-normative; §58 outcomes): `reject` on a missing stack; `reject` without
the administrative right of §36 (DS2-1); otherwise `ok`, metadata only (no right created, §36), the
identifier is fresh. -/
inductive MarkStep (j : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → MarkStep j D .reject
  | static {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → ¬ AdminRight D.kern st → MarkStep j D .reject
  | ok {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → AdminRight D.kern st →
      MarkStep j D (.ok ⟨D.kern, D.stacks.set j (markMeta j st D.fresh), D.fresh + 1⟩)

/-- `mark_rejects_without_right` (DS-v2, non-normative, DS2-1: `mark` requires `AdminRight` on the
stack, else `reject`; §36, §58): on an existing stack without the administrative right of §36,
`mark` has the outcome `reject` and no other. -/
theorem mark_rejects_without_right {j : Nat} {D : DState} {st : Stack}
    (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) (ha : ¬ AdminRight D.kern st) :
    MarkStep j D .reject ∧ ∀ o, MarkStep j D o → o = .reject := by
  refine ⟨.static hst ha, fun o ho => ?_⟩
  cases ho with
  | noStack => rfl
  | static => rfl
  | ok h ha' => rw [hst] at h; cases h; exact absurd ha' ha

/-! ## `rewind` (DS-v2) -/

/-- Metadata after `rewind m` (DS-v2, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §78 on §46 metadata):
the cells above `m` return to available (the top returns to the top of `m`), the blocks from that
top are forgotten, `m` and every later mark are removed. -/
def rewindMeta (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Stack :=
  { st with
    top := m.top
    blocks := st.blocks.filter fun x => decide (x.base < m.top)
    marks := st.marks.takeWhile fun x => decide (x ≠ m) }

/-- `rewind(j, m)` (DS-v2, non-normative): `reject` on a missing stack; `fail`, the state
unchanged, on a dead or foreign mark, a mark of a dead stack included (DS2-3), before the right;
`reject` without the administrative right of §36; then the derived `reset` of Part XIV on the cells
above `m`: `split` of `internal` on them (O2), which rejects when an active authority derived from
`internal` covers one of them (`rewind_rejects_live_above`), and `release` of the derived authority
(O3); `ok`: the cells return to available, `m` and the later marks are removed. -/

- `cd formal && ~/.elan/bin/lake env lean Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean` gives exit 0 with no errors or warnings.
- The file contains no sorry, admit, native_decide, axiom, noncomputable or set_option.
- `#print axioms` was run on all 123 declarations from the scratch copy /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref/v01/ds/DataStackAx.lean. The output is in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref/v01/ds/axioms.txt. Every one uses only propext and Quot.sound, or a subset; none uses Classical.choice.
- Not checked: Arena.lean and Refinement.lean have uncommitted edits by other agents. I compiled against their 09:13 build. Their diff only adds theorems, so nothing I use changed.

Spec passages read and implemented (v0.1): §36, §38, §42, §46, §47, §56, §58, §61, §62, §63 (only for the transfer in the witness), §65, §76.1–§76.6, §77.1–§77.4, §82, and the Part XIV preamble. Arbitration items: Q11 (a)–(f), Q23, Q27 (a), Q28 (c).

Each item and the theorem that now states it (paths are in formal/Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean):
- **DS2-1** (`mark` needs AdminRight): `MarkStep` (:206) has a new `static` reject case, and `ok` now requires `AdminRight`. Theorem `mark_rejects_without_right` (:215). Hypotheses: the stack exists and `¬ AdminRight`. Conclusion: `reject` and no other outcome. Example: `Witness.mark_without_right` (:1427). The runs `d5_reach` and `d7_reach` also exercise `mark` with the right.
- **DS2-2** (`grow` stores into the place that currently holds `b`):
  - New `holderPlace` (:340). `GrowStep` (:355) reads it on the state before the step. `growBlk` (:329) and `growMeta` (:333) take the destination `d` and record it in the block metadata.
  - `grow_same_base` (:1103). Hypothesis: an `ok` grow. It now also states `holderPlace D.kern b = some d`, and that the new authority is held by `.place d`.
  - `grow_keeps_prefix_bytes` (:1193). Hypotheses: an `ok` grow, the stack exists, `b` is a block. It now also states `holderPlace D.kern b = some d` and stores to `d`.
  - `DReach.grow_holder` (:836). Hypotheses: `DReach`, the stack exists, `b` is a block. It proves a holding place always exists, using the new invariant `BlocksHeld` (:754, with `DStep.blocksHeld` :771 and `DReach.blocksHeld` :827).
  - Example: `Witness.grow_follows_holder` (:1452). Block 5 is transferred from place 4 to place 5; `grow` is `ok` and stores into 5, and place 4 stays `Moved`.
- **DS2-3** (dead stack invalidates its marks):
  - `LiveMark` (:108) gains a kernel-state argument and the conjunct `Active internal`. So `RewindStep.dead` (:241) gives `fail` for a mark of a dead stack, before the right is checked.
  - `rewind_dead_stack_fails` (:1059). Hypotheses: the stack exists and its `internal` is inactive. Conclusion: `fail` and no other outcome.
  - `rewind_dead_fails` (:1043) now takes `¬ LiveMark` instead of `m ∉ st.marks`. That is a stronger theorem, not a weaker one.
  - Example: `Witness.dead_stack_marks_fail` (:1512).
- **Readings now decided:**
  - Push without room is `fail`: `PushStep.fail`, example `Witness.push_no_room` (:1403).
  - `grow` of a `b` that is not a block is `reject`: `GrowStep.noBlock`.
  - §76.5 applies to `newStack`: `NewStackPre.base`, example `Witness.newStack_value_uninit` (:1472). Its docstring now also cites §76.6, as the arena review asked.
  - A dead or foreign mark is `fail` before the right: `RewindStep.dead` and `rewind_dead_fails`, example `Witness.dead_mark_before_right` (:1395).
  - §36 applies to `rewind`: `RewindStep.static` and `rewind_ok_iff` (:870, hypothesis `DReach` only), example `Witness.rewind_needs_right` (:1487).
  - A missing stack index is `reject`: the `noStack` constructors.
  - `RewindStep.det` (:260) is re-proved.
- **O6.a** (the contract): `MarkStep`, `RewindStep`, `PushStep`, `GrowStep`, `InPlace`, `LiveMark`, `rewind_ok_iff`, `rewind_dead_fails`, `rewind_dead_stack_fails`, `mark_rejects_without_right`.
- **O6.b:**
  - `rewind_rejects_live_above` (:522). Hypotheses: the stack exists; `LiveMark D.kern j st m` (now includes a live stack, per DS2-3); an active authority derived from `internal` covers a cell above the mark.
  - `rewind_keeps_older_marks` (:548). Hypotheses: an `ok` rewind, the stack exists, `marks = pre ++ m :: post` with `m ∉ pre`.
  - `mark_no_aba` (:1069). Hypotheses: `MarksWF D` (still an explicit hypothesis, as before), an `ok` rewind, a later run, `m'` in `m :: post`.
- **O6.c:** `grow_same_base` and `grow_keeps_prefix_bytes` as above; `grow_keeps_prefix_init` (:1140) keeps its statement.

Removed: `Witness.reading_order` (split into `dead_mark_before_right`, `push_no_room` and `reading_grow_zero`), `reading_mark`, `reading_grow_dst`, `reading_newStack`, `reading_rewind_right`. Kept as an open reading: `reading_above`.

Fixed: `grow_keeps_prefix_bytes` no longer elaborated, because the refinement now implements `storeOps` through `writeOps`; its proof is updated.

open: DS-R3, for the user: a missing stack index is still `reject` for rewind, mark, push and grow (the `noStack` constructors). Q28 does not address it.

DS-R1, DS-R4, DS-R6 and DS-R8 are not named in Q11, Q27 or Q28, although Q23 says DS-R1 to DS-R13 are decided by them. The current readings are kept. `Witness.reading_above` (DS-R1) and `Witness.reading_grow_zero` (DS-R4) stay as reading witnesses.

DS2-2 representation choice: when no place holds `b` after an accepted release (it is held by a frame), `GrowStep.noHolder` gives `reject`. It is placed among the static checks, before the in-place `fail`. `DReach.grow_holder` proves this case never happens on library-reachable states. `b`'s holder is read on the state before the step; `releaseEff` does not change holders.

Statements changed by the contract, not to make a proof go through, for the reviewer to check: `LiveMark` (new state argument and liveness conjunct), and therefore the hypothesis of `rewind_rejects_live_above`; `grow_same_base` and `grow_keeps_prefix_bytes` (the destination is `holderPlace`, not `Blk.dst`); `rewind_dead_fails` (generalized from `m ∉ st.marks` to `¬ LiveMark`).
`mark_no_aba` still takes `MarksWF D` as an explicit hypothesis. No reachable corollary was added; it would be one line using `DReach.marksWF`.

Corpus/DataStack.lean will no longer elaborate: `LiveMark` and `growMeta` take more arguments, `MarkStep` and `GrowStep` have more constructor arguments, and five witnesses were removed or renamed. This belongs to the corpus phase; I did not touch it.
The module has no witness for DS-R5 (`grow` of a `b` that is not a block is `reject`). Its example is `Corpus.DataStack.DS03`.
